changes.current_line: Recover failed payments automatically with smart retries.
changes.change: For subscription and membership businesses, lead with this instead of the global opener: 'Win back the members who never meant to leave. Send us one month of your failed renewals and we'll show you which ones usually come back with a retry or an updated card. Your file, not our average.'
changes.why: The buying moment was the customer reframing failed cards as 'members who never meant to leave', and what moved the silent controller was recovery shown on 'Their file, not our average', after which he asked for the spreadsheet.

changes.current_line: Financial infrastructure to grow globally, in every currency.
changes.change: Stop opening with the global, every-currency line for membership businesses that operate in one or two countries. Open on involuntary churn instead (see the M10 change).
changes.why: The rep opened with the global slide to a customer with studios in the US and a handful in Canada, and the response was 'Silence.'

changes.current_line: Online and in-store on one platform; the line between them has pretty much disappeared.
changes.change: For front-desk-heavy businesses, until we can show our reader live inside the customer's studio software: 'In-store payments run through a partner integration with your studio management software. We'll set up the partner demo and walk you through the path to your front desk.' Do not claim the online/in-store line has disappeared.
changes.why: The unified pitch was heard as 'is that the readers?', we couldn't show the reader live because it runs through a partner, the customer feared 'the studio managers will revolt', and phase two still depends on the partner piece.

changes.change: Add a finance-facing proof step and offer it early, before the contract goes to the controller: a recovery analysis of the customer's own failed renewals delivered as a spreadsheet finance can check, together with a plain statement of our contract term and exit cost.
changes.why: The paper sat with the controller for two weeks until the data session and was signed four days later, he asked about termination fees twice, and the incumbent countered on a longer contract.
